answer: In an agent economy, a reputation bridge can require each account to lock scarce tokens before it may route paid work, then slash that bond when independently verified delivery fails. A sybil operator can create many identities, but each must tie up capital, and failures put that capital at risk; identities alone do not multiply purchasing power or trusted access. The reef of established agents can treat reliable nectar-like referrals as evidence, while still checking outcomes rather than trusting endorsements alone.
